newsitem.title: UK: Lonrho in preliminary merger talks with JCI.
newsitem.headline: Lonrho in preliminary merger talks with JCI.

text.p: British conglomerate Lonrho Plc said on Monday that it has had preliminary talks with South Africa's JCI to identify any benefits of a combining the two groups.
However, it said that it has not tabled or considered any merger proposals.
Lonrho said in a statement, "If considered appropriate, Lonrho will continue discussions with JCI and will make a further announcement only if there are any significant developments."
The company was responding to newspaper reports that it was in merger talks with JCI in a move that would create one of the world's largest mining companies.
The Sunday Telegraph said that under the proposals Lonrho would bid for JCI, which is valued at 900 million pounds ($1.5 billion), and the new company would be quoted in London and Johannesburg.
The newspaper said the plan envisaged Anglo American Corporation of South Africa swopping its 28 percent stake in Lonrho, plus some cash, for Lonrho's 41 percent in Ghanaian gold mine Ashanti.
